item5_V7.finding: fp32 native row sums (kernels.cu reduce_lastdim_kernel: 256 threads x R/256 sequential adds + 8-level tree) give an accumulation depth of R/256 + 7; at R = 2^20 that is 4103 roundings (bound ~2.4e-4 relative), and the review's clustered witness drifts the mean by 4e-5 -> threshold outside the 2e-5 band.
item5_V7.fix: quant._row_sum (statistics block only): rows with S <= 8192 keep the engine's single-pass row sum (depth <= 39, unchanged bytes); S > 8192 use a two-level blocked sum -- reshape to 4096-key blocks, sum each block (depth <= 23), then sum the partials with the same rule (recursive), plus the < 4096-key remainder summed natively and added once. Used for BOTH moments (mean of u, centered sum of squares). The definition is unchanged (same population mean, centered variance, threshold, >=); only the summation order/precision changes.
item5_V7.why_not_fp64: the engine has no float64 dtype (tensor_cuda/include/tc/core.h:30 enum DType: Float32, Float16, Int64, Bool, Uint8, BFloat16); fp64 accumulation would need a kernel change (kernels.cu is not writable in this order).
item5_V7.bound_reasoning: recursive-summation bound |err| <= gamma_k * sum|x| (Higham 2002 ch.4) with k = depth: S <= 8192: k <= 39 (2.3e-6); 8192 < S <= 2^20: k <= 23 + 8 + 1 = 32 (1.9e-6); for u >= 0 and z >= 0 the threshold error is <= ~6.3e-6 * thr in the worst case, inside the 2e-5 band. Reasoning, not measurement; the sweep is the measurement.
item5_V7.memory: S % 4096 == 0 (incl. S = 2^20): reshape views only, plus B*H*L*S/4096 fp32 partials per moment (1 KiB per row at S = 2^20); otherwise one transient slice copy of the first nb*4096 keys per moment (<= 4*B*H*L*S bytes, freed before the next moment).
